transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Priya Nair
Hi! I'm Priya, from Nair's Kitchen Tiffin & Catering. Nice to meet you! What do you need from me?
Birdie

Nice to meet you, Priya! Lovely name for a business, by the way. To start, could you tell me a bit about what's prompting you to want a chatbot — what's the main problem or headache you're hoping it solves?
Priya Nair

Aww thank you! Um, mainly it's just... people message me on WhatsApp all day asking "how much for tiffin" or "can you do catering for 50 people this weekend" and I'm cooking with my hands all messy and can't reply fast, haha. So maybe something that can just answer the basic questions for me so I don't lose customers while I'm busy? Though honestly I'm not 100% sure what all it can do, that's why I wanted to talk to you first.
Birdie

That makes total sense, Priya — messy hands and a phone buzzing nonstop is rough! Before we dig into details, do you have any real WhatsApp chats or screenshots of customers asking you things like the tiffin/catering questions you mentioned? If you can drop a few into the 'uploads' folder next to this program, just tell me when you're done — seeing real questions helps me ask much better questions. If you don't have any handy, that's totally fine too, we can just continue.
Priya Nair

Oh, um, let me think... I probably have some on my phone but I'm not sure how to get them into a folder thing, haha. Let's just say the usual ones are like "how much for tiffin," "do you deliver to my area," and "can you do catering for a party" — those come up all the time. I'll try to add screenshots later if I find time, but maybe we just continue for now?
Birdie
No worries at all, Priya, whenever you have time is fine! Let's dig in — could you tell me your tiffin pricing (like per meal or per week/month) and roughly what areas you deliver to?
Priya Nair

Okay so, tiffin is usually somewhere between $12 and $15 a day, depends on the menu that day, like if there's extra sabzi or something. And if someone wants the whole month it's maybe $300-ish? But honestly could be more if they want extra roti, some people eat a lot haha.

For delivery, I don't really have a strict "area" — anything within like 5 miles is free, and outside that I just add a little extra, maybe $5 to $10, I don't have it fixed exactly, just depends how far and if Anjali's free that day to drive.
Birdie

Got it, thanks! Since pricing can shift a bit day to day, should the bot just give people a general range (like "$12-15 a day" or "free within 5 miles, a bit more beyond that") and let you confirm exact numbers yourself, or would you rather it always says "let me check and get back to you" for pricing questions?
Priya Nair

Hmm, maybe... a mix? Like for the basic tiffin price it can just say the range, $12-15, that's fine, people don't mind that. But for the bigger stuff, like party trays or catering for events, maybe it should just say "let me check and get back to you" because those really depend on what all they want, you know? I don't want it promising some number and then I'm losing money again, haha, that happens to me enough already.
Birdie

That makes a lot of sense, better safe than losing money! Now let's talk bookings — when someone wants to book catering for an event, how does that usually work? Do you take a deposit or any payment upfront to hold the date?
Priya Nair

Oh, um, no not really a formal deposit or anything, haha. Usually people just message me, tell me the date and how many people, and I say yes if I'm free, and we figure out payment after — Venmo or cash, mostly at the end or sometimes half before if they offer, I don't really ask for it strictly. I know I probably should ask for something upfront so people don't cancel last minute, but I just... haven't set that up. Maybe the bot could ask them the date and headcount at least, so I have that info before they even message me? That part I really need help with actually.
Birdie

That's a really common gap, and totally fixable! It sounds like right now you mainly just need the bot to collect the date and headcount for catering inquiries and pass that to you — rather than handling full booking and payment itself. Just to be clear on scope: would you like the bot to eventually handle full booking with payment collection (like taking a deposit through the chat), or keep it simpler for now — just gathering details, maybe sending reminders, and letting you handle payment separately like you do today?
Priya Nair

Yeah, let's keep it simple for now I think? Like just collect the date, how many people, maybe what kind of event it is, and then I'll message them back myself about payment and all. I don't think I'm ready for it to actually take money or anything, that feels like a big step, haha. Maybe later if it works out well we can add that part, but for now just the basic info gathering is enough, I think... unless you think it's easy to add the payment thing too? I don't know, whatever you think is easier to start with honestly.
Birdie

That's a smart way to start, Priya — simple and low-risk, and we can always add payment collection later once you're comfortable. Good call. Now, roughly how many messages or customer conversations do you think come in on WhatsApp in a typical week?
Priya Nair

Hmm, that's a good question... it really varies week to week, haha. Like some weeks it's quiet, maybe 20-30 messages total? But if it's near a festival or holiday season, oh my god, it can be like 60-70 easy, everyone wants tiffin or catering at the same time. I'd say... on average maybe 30-40? But don't quote me on that, I've never actually counted, I'm just guessing from feeling tired some weeks, haha.
Birdie
Good to know, thanks. Do you talk to your customers in English only, or do some conversations happen in another language too, like Hindi or Malayalam?
Priya Nair

Oh, mostly English, yeah. But sometimes older customers or aunties from the community will text in Hindi, or like, Manglish — mixing Malayalam and English, haha. Nothing too heavy usually, just small phrases like "enthada rate" or something, but I reply in English mostly and they understand. I don't think we need anything fancy for language, just... maybe if it could understand a few common words like that? Not sure if that's even possible, haha.
Birdie

Got it, that's helpful context. Now, how will you know this chatbot is actually working well for you — like, what would success look like a couple months in? Fewer missed messages, more catering bookings, something else?
Priya Nair

Oh hmm, good question... I guess mainly if I'm not missing messages while I'm cooking, that would already feel like a win, haha. Like right now sometimes I see a message at 9pm and someone wanted lunch tiffin, too late! So if the bot just catches those and answers basic stuff, that alone would make me happy.

But also, I guess... more bookings would be nice too? Like if catering inquiries turn into actual events instead of just people asking and disappearing. Though honestly even just less stress for me, not checking phone every five minutes, that's success also, haha. I don't have like a number in mind, just... less chaos I think. Does that make sense or is that too vague, sorry!
Birdie

That makes total sense, no need for exact numbers — 'less chaos and no missed messages' is a perfectly good goal! One more important thing: are there times the bot should immediately hand things off to you directly, like an urgent same-day order, a complaint, or something it just can't answer?
Priya Nair

Yeah, definitely — like if someone messages saying they need tiffin literally today or like in an hour, the bot should probably just tell them to call me or text me directly instead of trying to sort it out, because that needs a real yes/no from me fast. Same thing if someone's upset, like complaining the food was late or something was wrong with their order — I don't want the bot trying to handle that, just send it straight to me, I'll deal with it personally.

And umm, also if it's some big last-minute event thing, like "can you do 80 people tomorrow" — that's a hard no most of the time but I'd still want to see it myself just in case I'm free that day, you know? Those last-minute ones are tricky, sometimes I say yes anyway if I'm not too tired, haha. So maybe anything urgent or emotional, just push it to me directly instead of the bot trying to answer.
Birdie

Got it — urgent, emotional, or big last-minute requests all go straight to you, that's clear. Do you currently use any tools alongside WhatsApp, like a calendar app, an order spreadsheet, or Venmo/payment app, that the bot might need to work alongside or check?
Priya Nair

Oh, um, not really any fancy tools, haha. I mean I use Venmo for payment like I said, but for tracking orders or bookings... honestly it's mostly just in my head, or sometimes I scribble it on a notepad in the kitchen, which is probably not great, I know. I don't have like a Google calendar or spreadsheet or anything set up properly. Anjali sometimes texts me reminders too if I forget something, haha. So I guess the bot wouldn't really have anything to "check" against, it'd just be collecting new info mostly? Unless you think I should start using some simple calendar thing alongside it, I don't know, whatever's easier.
Birdie

That's totally fine, lots of small businesses run this way! We could suggest a simple calendar down the line, but for now the bot can just collect info without needing to check anything. Two last practical questions, starting with this one: do you have a rough budget in mind for building this chatbot?
Priya Nair

Oh gosh, budget... I haven't really thought about like a number, honestly. I don't have some big marketing budget or anything set aside, it's just me and my kitchen, haha. I guess... something reasonable? Like whatever's normal for a small business like mine, not the fancy expensive kind. If you can give me like a range, small/medium/big option, that would help me figure out what I can actually do. I don't want to say a number and then feel silly if it's way off, you know?
Birdie

Totally understandable, no wrong answers here! Since we're keeping the scope simple for now (just WhatsApp auto-replies and info collection, no payments), that usually lands on the smaller/more affordable end compared to a full booking app — I'll note that for the developer to give you options. Last question: do you have any particular timeline in mind, like wanting this ready before a busy season or event?
Priya Nair

Oh timeline, hmm... well there's always some festival or Onam or Diwali coming up when things get crazy busy, haha, so if it could be ready before the next busy stretch that'd be nice. But honestly I don't want to promise myself a date either, because — okay don't judge me — I've been saying I'll make a website "this year" for like two years now and never did it, haha. So maybe just... whenever it's reasonably ready is fine? No huge rush, but sooner is obviously better than later so I stop losing messages at 9pm.
Birdie

Thanks, Priya, I think I've got a good picture now! Here's a quick summary to confirm:

• You run Nair's Kitchen Tiffin & Catering, and want a WhatsApp bot to handle the flood of messages you can't answer while cooking.
• It should answer common questions: tiffin pricing ($12-15/day, ~$300/month, varies with extras) and delivery (free within 5 miles, +$5-10 beyond depending on distance/driver availability).
• For catering/party inquiries, it should NOT quote prices — just say you'll follow up — since those vary too much.
• For catering leads, it should collect date, headcount, and event type, then hand that info to you rather than trying to book or take payment. This is the 'simple' scope for now, no payment collection yet — you're open to adding deposits/payment later once you're comfortable.
• Urgent same-day requests, complaints, and big last-minute events (like '80 people tomorrow') should always be escalated straight to you, not handled by the bot.
• You currently have no deposit/cancellation policy — payment is informal (Venmo/cash, sometimes half upfront) — and no calendar or tracking tool beyond memory and notepads.
• Volume is roughly 20-40 messages/week normally, spiking to 60-70 during festivals.
• Mostly English, with occasional Hindi/Manglish phrases — happy to see what's feasible there.
• Success = not missing messages, more catering inquiries turning into bookings, and less stress for you.
• Budget: open to guidance on small/medium/large options, nothing fancy needed since we're starting simple.
• Timeline: no hard deadline, ideally before the next festival season, but no pressure.

Does all that sound right, or is there anything you'd like to change?
Priya Nair

Yeah, that all sounds right to me! Haha, you explained it back way more organized than how I said it. Only tiny thing — the party trays, I don't think we talked about those in the summary, but that's okay, that probably falls under the "no pricing, just follow up" bucket too, right? Other than that, looks good, I think you got me pretty well!
Birdie

Perfect, thanks so much Priya! I've got everything I need. Here's what happens next: I'll pass these notes along to the development team, and they'll put together a plan and some options (including that small/medium/large pricing guidance) for your simple WhatsApp helper bot. Thanks for being so open and detailed — this is going to save you a lot of 9pm stress!

brief.problem_to_solve: Owner cooks hands-on and can't reply quickly to WhatsApp messages asking about tiffin pricing and catering availability, risking lost customers.
brief.target_audience: People ordering daily tiffin and those inquiring about catering for events
integrations: None currently - no calendar, spreadsheet, or order tracking tool in use; payments via Venmo/cash handled manually by owner; owner open to adding a simple calendar tool alongside the bot later
brief.conversation_volume: Roughly 20-30 messages/week in quiet times, up to 60-70/week during festivals/holidays; average guess ~30-40/week (not precisely counted)
languages: Occasional Manglish (Malayalam-English mix) phrases from older/community customers
brief.success_criteria: Not missing time-sensitive messages (e.g. late tiffin orders that come in too late to fulfill); catering inquiries converting to actual bookings instead of going cold; overall less stress/chaos for owner from constantly checking phone. No specific numeric target, framed as 'less chaos.'
brief.budget: No specific number in mind; wants a simple small/medium/large range suggestion appropriate for a small solo-run food business, not a large marketing-style budget
brief.timeline: No firm deadline; would like it ready before the next busy festival season (e.g. Onam/Diwali) if possible, but owner is wary of self-imposed deadlines given past experience; general preference is 'sooner is better' with no hard date
services_and_pricing: Daily tiffin: $12-$15/day depending on menu (extra sabzi etc. changes price)
Monthly tiffin: approx $300, but can be more if customer wants extras like extra roti
Party trays fall under same treatment as catering: no fixed price quoted by bot, handled as a follow-up item
faq_answers: Common recurring customer questions: 'how much for tiffin', 'do you deliver to my area', 'can you do catering for a party'
business_policies: Delivery within 5 miles is free; beyond that, extra fee of roughly $5-$10 depending on distance and driver (Anjali) availability - not a fixed rate

For tiffin, bot can quote general price range ($12-15/day); for catering/party trays, bot should NOT quote a price and instead say 'let me check and get back to you' since those vary too much and owner has lost money quoting wrong before

No formal deposit currently required for catering bookings; payment (Venmo or cash) usually settled after the event or sometimes half upfront if customer offers, but not strictly enforced - owner acknowledges she 'probably should' ask for upfront payment to prevent last-minute cancellations but hasn't set this up
escalation_rules: Catering/party tray pricing requests should be escalated to Priya rather than answered by bot
Same-day/urgent tiffin requests (e.g. needed within the hour) should be escalated immediately to Priya directly (call/text) rather than handled by bot
Complaints or upset customers (e.g. late food, wrong order) should be escalated straight to Priya, not handled by bot

Large last-minute event requests (e.g. '80 people tomorrow') should be escalated to Priya even though usually a hard no, because she sometimes says yes depending on her own energy/availability - owner wants to personally review these rather than have bot auto-decline
open_items: Owner may share WhatsApp screenshots later if she finds time to upload them
Tiffin and delivery pricing are variable/not fixed (depends on menu extras, distance, driver availability) - need to decide how bot should quote a range or escalate to owner for exact price
No deposit/cancellation policy currently exists for catering; owner wants to add one but hasn't decided terms yet - needs follow-up

Scope decision: starting simple (bot just collects date, headcount, event type for catering inquiries, no payment handling); owner is open to adding payment/deposit collection later once she sees how it works
Conversation volume is a rough guess, not measured (20-70/week depending on season)
Unclear if/how well bot can handle occasional Hindi/Manglish phrases - owner unsure if this is feasible, needs follow-up on how robust this should be
Owner has no existing calendar/tracking tool; open to adding a simple one alongside the bot but undecided
Budget undefined - owner wants guidance on small/medium/large pricing tiers rather than committing to a number upfront
Timeline is soft/aspirational (before next festival season) rather than a hard deadline
additional_notes: Chosen initial scope: simple info-gathering bot (not full booking/payment app) - collects date, headcount, event type for catering inquiries, then owner follows up personally about payment
Order tracking currently informal (memory, notepad, reminders from Anjali) - no digital system in place
